refresh_policy.rationale: Collection reuses the owner's signed-in mountainproject.com session and makes three same-origin GETs per run, one second apart: the profile page and the site's own CSV exports of the owner's ticks and to-do list. First collection and an expired session need the owner to sign in through the browser handoff.

public_listing.rationale: Built 2026-11-11. The parsers were checked against the real tick and to-do exports and the profile page of a project-owned test account (5 ticks, 3 to-dos; counts matched); a full connector run through the browser handoff on a real account has not been done yet.

pageshim.login_message: Sign in to Mountain Project (email, onX, Facebook or Apple), then return here.

streams.name: profile
streams.description: The owner's own Mountain Project profile: name, location, join date, picture and the profile's tick and to-do counts. Age, gender and points are not collected.

display.label: Your Mountain Project profile
display.detail: Display name, profile location, member-since date, profile picture link, and how many ticks and to-dos the profile counts.

display_name.description: The name shown on the profile.

avatar_url.description: The profile picture URL; null when none is shown.

location.description: The location the owner put on their profile.

member_since.description: The day the account was created, as the profile states it.

tick_count.description: How many ticks the profile counts; null when the profile shows no count.

todo_count.description: How many to-do routes the profile counts; null when the profile shows no count.

streams.name: ticks
streams.description: Every climb the owner logged (ticked) on Mountain Project, one record per tick, read from the site's own tick CSV export: the day, the route with its grade, type, location and length, how it was climbed, pitches, the owner's notes, stars and suggested grade. Every run re-reads the whole export. The time range applies to the tick's day.

display.label: Your ticks
display.detail: Each climb you logged: date, route, grade, route type, location, style and lead style, pitches, your notes, your stars and your suggested grade.

id.description: <route_id>:<date>:<n>. The export carries no tick id; n counts the owner's ticks of the same route on the same day, in export order (newest first), from 1. Adding or deleting one such tick shifts the others' n.

route_id.description: Mountain Project's route id, from the route URL.

rating.description: The route's grade as Mountain Project shows it, for example "5.10a", "V4" or "5.11 V1+".

rating_code.description: Mountain Project's numeric sort code for the grade.

location.description: The route's location path, outermost area first (state or country down to the crag).

avg_stars.description: The community's average star rating of the route.

your_stars.description: The owner's own star rating of the route; null when they gave none.

route_type.description: Route types, for example Trad, Sport, TR, Boulder, Alpine, Ice.

your_rating.description: The grade the owner suggested for the route; null when they gave none.

length_ft.description: The route's length in feet, as the export states it.

style.description: How the route was climbed: Lead, Follow, TR, Solo, Send, Flash or Attempt. Null when the owner left it blank.

lead_style.description: For a lead: Onsight, Flash, Redpoint, Pinkpoint or Fell/Hung. Null otherwise.

notes.description: The owner's notes on the tick.

streams.name: saved_routes
streams.description: The routes on the owner's Mountain Project to-do list, one record per route, read from the site's own to-do CSV export: the route with its grade, type, location, length and pitch count, plus the owner's stars and suggested grade when given. Every run re-reads the whole list. A route the owner removes from the list is not reported as deleted.

display.label: Your to-do list
display.detail: Each route on your to-do list: name, grade, route type, location, length, pitches, average stars, and your own stars and grade if you gave them.

id.description: The route id; a route is on the to-do list at most once.

route_id.description: Mountain Project's route id, from the route URL.

rating.description: The route's grade as Mountain Project shows it, for example "5.10a", "V4" or "5.11 V1+".

rating_code.description: Mountain Project's numeric sort code for the grade.

location.description: The route's location path, outermost area first (state or country down to the crag).

avg_stars.description: The community's average star rating of the route.

your_stars.description: The owner's own star rating of the route; null when they gave none.

route_type.description: Route types, for example Trad, Sport, TR, Boulder, Alpine, Ice.

your_rating.description: The grade the owner suggested for the route; null when they gave none.

length_ft.description: The route's length in feet, as the export states it.

reason_display_messages.stream_collection_failed: Mountain Project could not be read completely this time. Nothing already saved was lost.
reason_display_messages.records_unreadable: Some rows of your Mountain Project export could not be read and were not saved. Everything else was saved.
reason_display_messages.export_shorter_than_profile_count: Your Mountain Project export had fewer entries than your profile counts, so this list may be incomplete. Everything in the export was saved.
reason_display_messages.mountain_project_auth_failed: Your Mountain Project session has ended. Sign in to Mountain Project again to continue.
reason_display_messages.mountain_project_interrupted: The Mountain Project page was closed or left during the sync. Sync again to continue.
reason_display_messages.mountain_project_rate_limited: Mountain Project is limiting requests right now. The sync will try again later.
reason_display_messages.mountain_project_server_error: Mountain Project is having trouble right now. The sync will try again later.
reason_display_messages.mountain_project_network_error: Mountain Project could not be reached. Check your connection; the sync will try again later.
reason_display_messages.mountain_project_invalid_payload: Mountain Project answered in a format this connector does not recognize. A connector update is needed.
